```{r, Prepare data}

library(openxlsx)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(sjPlot)
library(knitr)
library(estimatr)
library(car)
library(sandwich)
library(gee)
library(rstatix)
library(psych)
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(emmeans)
library(xtable)
library(Superpower)
library(pwranova)

# Load in the data set for blame graphs
df_long <- read.xlsx("Victim Blame S1-3 LONG 2026.11.11.xlsx")
df_wide <- read.xlsx("Victim Blame S1-3 WIDE 2025.11.11.xlsx")

df_long$polGen <- as.factor(df_long$polGen)
df_long$session <- as.factor(df_long$session)

df_wide$polGen <- as.factor(df_wide$polGen)
df_wide$session <- as.factor(df_wide$session)

# Rename variables

# Target
df_long$Target <- ifelse(df_long$VictVsPerp == 0, "Victim", "Perpetrator")
df_long$Target <- factor(df_long$Target, levels = c("Perpetrator", "Victim"))

table(df_long$VictVsPerp)
table(df_long$Target)

# Sex
df_long$Sex <- ifelse(df_long$sexBin == 0, "Female", 
                      ifelse(df_long$sexBin == 1, "Male", df_long$sexBin))
df_long$Sex <- factor(df_long$Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))

df_wide$Sex <- ifelse(df_wide$sexBin == 0, "Female", 
                      ifelse(df_wide$sexBin == 1, "Male", df_wide$sexBin))
df_wide$Sex <- factor(df_wide$Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))

table(df_wide$sexBin)
table(df_wide$Sex)

# Ideology
df_long$Ideology <- ifelse(df_long$polGen == 0, "Liberal",
                           ifelse(df_long$polGen == 1, "Moderate", 
                           ifelse(df_long$polGen == 2, "Conservative", df_long$polGen)))

df_long$Ideology <- factor(df_long$Ideology, levels = c("Liberal", "Moderate", "Conservative"))

df_wide$Ideology <- ifelse(df_wide$polGen == 0, "Liberal",
                           ifelse(df_wide$polGen == 1, "Moderate", 
                           ifelse(df_wide$polGen == 2, "Conservative", df_wide$polGen)))

df_wide$Ideology <- factor(df_wide$Ideology, levels = c("Liberal", "Moderate", "Conservative"))

table(df_wide$polGen)
table(df_wide$Ideology)

# Session
df_long$Wave <- ifelse(df_long$session == 0, "Wave 1", 
                          ifelse(df_long$session == 1, "Wave 2", "Wave 3"))
df_long$Wave <- factor(df_long$Wave, levels = c("Wave 1", "Wave 2", "Wave 3"))

df_wide$Wave <- ifelse(df_wide$session == 0, "Wave 1", 
                          ifelse(df_wide$session == 1, "Wave 2", "Wave 3"))
df_wide$Wave <- factor(df_wide$Wave, levels = c("Wave 1", "Wave 2", "Wave 3"))

table(df_wide$Wave)
table(df_wide$session)

# Threat
df_wide$Threat <- df_wide$fear

```

```{r, Mixed ANOVA with VB data}

# Omnibus
mixed_anova <- anova_test(
  data = df_long,
  dv = selfBlame,
  wid = RespondentID,
  between = session,
  within = Target
)

get_anova_table(mixed_anova) # Matches SPSS

# Means and SDs
table_ms_sds <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Target, session) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    M = mean(selfBlame, na.rm = T),
    SD = sd(selfBlame, na.rm = T),
    n = sum(!is.na(selfBlame)),
    .groups = "drop" # ungroup
    )

table_ms_sds

```


# Power analyses based on mixed ANOVA

```{r, Post-hoc power analysis}

# Using the Superpower package (Caldwell et al., 2022)
# https://aaroncaldwell.us/SuperpowerBook/repeated-measures-anova.html#multivariate-anova-manova

# Set up corr matrix of victim and perp within each session
df_session1 <- df_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(session == 0)

df_session2 <- df_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(session == 1)

df_session3 <- df_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(session == 2)

table(df_session1$session)
table(df_session2$session)
table(df_session3$session)

cor.test(df_session1$selfPerp, df_session1$selfVict) # -0.74
r_s1 <- -0.74
cor.test(df_session2$selfPerp, df_session2$selfVict) # -0.73
r_s2 <- -0.73
cor.test(df_session3$selfPerp, df_session3$selfVict) # -0.73
r_s3 <- -0.73

# Assume corr of 0 for between-subjects effects

# Create corr matrix
rho_mat <- diag(6)

rho_mat[1, 4] <- r_s1
rho_mat[4, 1] <- r_s1

rho_mat[2, 5] <- r_s2
rho_mat[5, 2] <- r_s2

rho_mat[3, 6] <- r_s3
rho_mat[6, 3] <- r_s3

rho_mat

# Define parameters 
mu <- table_ms_sds$M 
n <- 361 # 1083/3, function won't take unequal n
sd <- table_ms_sds$SD
alpha_level <- 0.05
labelnames = c("Target", "Perpetator", "Victim",
               "Session", "S1", "S2", "S3")

# Run function
design_result <- ANOVA_design("2w*3b",
                              n = n,
                              sd = sd,
                              mu = mu,
                              r = -.74,
                              labelnames = labelnames,
                              plot = TRUE)

exact_result <- ANOVA_exact(design_result, verbose = FALSE,
                            correction = "none",
                            alpha_level = .05)

exact_result$main_results # Omnibus, matches SPSS for omnibus 
view(exact_result$pc_results) # Pairwise comparisons

```

# Sensitivity Analyses

```{r, MDE for wave*target interaction}

# Use pwranova package (Muto, 2026)
# https://mutopsy.github.io/pwranova/

sens_interaction <- pwranova(
  nlevels_b = 3,       
  nlevels_w = 2,       
  n_total = 1083,
  alpha = .05,
  power = .80,
  cohensf = NULL,      
  epsilon = 1,
  target = "B1:W1"    
)

sens_interaction

# Cohens f - 0.09 (Matches g*power where can specify corrs between repeated measures)
# Partial eta squared - 0.008

```

```{r, MDE for pairwise comparisons between waves}

# Hold sample size consistent and vary means
# Want to see a difference between waves 1 and 2 on perp and vict blame

# Original means 
mu_original <- c(
  3.507650, 3.468976, 3.331378,
  1.720184, 1.760306, 1.948283)

# Perp: Decrease session 2 and 3 by .05
# Vict: Increase session 2 and 3 by .05

delta <- 0.05

# Define parameters 
mu <- mu_original + c(
  0, -delta, -delta, 
  0,  delta,  delta
)
# Don't necessarily need to alter session 3 but do so if want to maintain dif between wave 2 and 3
# Note that it means dif between wave 1 vs 3 is exaggerated
# But all we really care about is wave 1 vs 2

n <- 361 # 1083/3, function won't take unequal n
sd <- table_ms_sds$SD
alpha_level <- 0.05
labelnames = c("Target", "Perpetator", "Victim",
               "Session", "S1", "S2", "S3"
               )

# Run function
mean_dif_increase_result1 <- ANOVA_design("2w*3b",
                              n = n,
                              sd = sd,
                              mu = mu,
                              r = rho_mat,
                              labelnames = labelnames,
                              plot = TRUE)

mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result1 <- ANOVA_exact(mean_dif_increase_result1, verbose = FALSE,
                                                     correction = "none",
                                                     alpha_level = .05)

mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result1$main_results # Omnibus, matches SPSS for omnibus 
view(mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result1$pc_results) # Pairwise comparisons

# Perp: 71.87 power
# Vict: 65.79 power

##

# Perp: Decrease session 2 and 3 by 0.067
# Vict: Increase session 2 and 3 by 0.067

delta <- 0.067

# Define parameters 
mu <- mu_original + c(
  0, -delta, -delta,
  0,  delta,  delta
)

# Run function
mean_dif_increase_result2 <- ANOVA_design("2w*3b",
                              n = n,
                              sd = sd,
                              mu = mu,
                              r = rho_mat,
                              labelnames = labelnames,
                              plot = TRUE)

mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result2 <- ANOVA_exact(mean_dif_increase_result2, verbose = FALSE,
                                                     correction = "none",
                                                     alpha_level = .05)

mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result2$main_results # Omnibus, matches SPSS for omnibus 
view(mean_dif_increase_result_exact_result2$pc_results) # Pairwise comparisons

# Perp: 85.67 power (d = -0.23)
# Vict: 80.32 power (d = 0.21)

# MDE ~ d = 0.21

```
